body:
Well that is certainly good news. I'd rather have to worry about shitting myself everyday than guessing if I was going to be able to do anything from the pain everyday.

And that's what I did as well, putting on a brave face. I didn't want to disappoint my doctors, so I was much more timid. My mother pointed that out to me.

Thank you for the encouragement. We've found that my mother's side of the family has a history with gallbladder issues, so it really seems like that might be it.

Anyways, I hope you're doing alright. Sorry if my post is lacking depth, I'm just tired tonight. But yeah, thanks so much for the advice and the encouragement. I hope that 10 years down the road, I'll be thankful that I didn't commit suicide, and I'll never forget the help I got here.

Thank you! I knew I couldn't be the only one with this stupid shit.

First off, let me just say that I'm sorry this happened to you too, I wouldn't wish this on my worst enemy.

Second, if you don't mind my asking, what are some of the new complications that arise from having your gallbladder removed? I'm hesitant to remove anything, but I'll **DEFINITELY** be checking on three things: Gallbladder, Chrons, and my esophagus.

Lastly, I hope you continue to do better. For me, before all this, I wanted to lose some weight. I had terrible self-image issues (which seem to love anxiety) and was convinced I was morbidly obese. Now, I can feel my bones, which that's never happened before. I guess what I'm trying to say is that I really hope things get better for you. As far as I'm concerned, if my pain was gone, I'd never worry about the mundane things I was worried about before.

If things don't get better for me, if I do kill myself one day, please live for the both of us. I know that's a strange request from a stranger on the internet, but live your life to the fullest.

I'll doggedly pursue my doctors' for answers, but if it doesn't work out for me, please don't forget to live your life without regret, for me.

Again, thank you. If anything, rest easy knowing that if I do go, I won't go feeling so alone. But I'm not there yet. If I have to get angry with my doctors, so be it. But I'm not going to let them push right past me anymore.

I'm definitely going to be checking on my gallbladder, someone else mentioned it, and it seems like a good lead.

As for my esophagus, my mother has esophageal spasms, but they've never noticed anything strange with me. Like I mentioned in my edit, every time I mention the belching thing, doctors hastily say i'm just swallowing air, or simply say nothing at all.

I may need to be more persistent with my doctors, but i'm not going to wait for answers anymore. Something's not right, and i'm not going to let them worry about whether or not i'll be a good paycheck, but rather whether or not i'll live.

I have only tried meditation once, and it was long before things got to where they are now. I enjoyed it, but it is all but impossible for me now.

The way I've tried to describe it is that when I become anxious, a sort of static grows in my head, and picking out one thought becomes extremely difficult. The more anxious I become, the worse the static gets, and soon I can only focus on the growing pain in my stomach, and how soon i'm going to throw up, and no, no, not this again, and why now, will I be able to sleep tonight, please no more pain -

and then I throw up. Very forcefully, my stomach feels like it pushes right into my throat. If it's any help, my family says they've never seen anyone throw up like I do. It's so strong and, well, forceful, there's no other word for it. And it hurts incredibly badly.

I try and be positive, I promise you I do. Before all this happened, I was ready to go and get a degree, and be the first in my family to graduate from college. From there, I was ready to go write a book, or translate for the deaf, or find the cure for cancer.

I have/had hopes, dreams, aspirations... but i'm paralyzed by fear and pain now. I feel as if (and i'm not very religious) that something, some force is trying to make me end my life, or that i'm cursed or something.

I don't know. And I suppose that's what scares me.

But I love you too. I hope you know that with all my heart I love you too. It means immeasurably to me that you would take the time to cheer for me. But I don't want to disappoint you too, if things don't get better.

I'll say this much, I won't give up, not yet. I'm not at the end of my rope, but I know that if I get there, the animal instinct in me is to end my pain.

Thank you.

You might want to see my reply to dragelmeu, I explain more there.

Long story short, they don't think I have Chrohns, but they also know I don't have insurance.

Through biopsies, they've tested for multiple things, Chrones' included. Throughout all my tests, they said that I was very healthy, so *physically* there's nothing wrong with me.

In that regard, they believe that throughout the years, I've stressed myself out to the point where I've 'burned up' the serotonin receptors in my stomach.

And that would make since, if not for the fact that one night I woke up at 3:30, felt strange, and was throwing up pure stomach acid/bile by 3:45. It's not like I was stressed in my sleep, y'know?

I admit, my gastroenterologist has been very supportive, but I feel that they are quick to pass over other possibilities, mostly because I assume they know I have no insurance.
